Cross-Validate Mixed-Effects Models

Source: R/cross_validate_mixed.R
cross_validate_mixed.Rd

Refit a mixed model in every analysis split and score the observations held out from it. A random intercept gives each group, such as a site, its own baseline drawn from a common distribution, which accounts for the similarity among repeated surveys of that group. Choose whether prediction is for groups represented in training or for wholly new groups. Response means and joint group log scores integrate over the shared group effect.

Usage

cross_validate_mixed(
  formula,
  data,
  folds,
  family = c("gaussian", "poisson", "binomial", "nbinom2", "Gamma"),
  prediction = c("new_group", "existing_group"),
  kernel_inputs = NULL,
  optim_args = list(),
  metrics = NULL,
  control = NULL,
  integration_tol = 1e-08,
  keep_fits = FALSE
)

Arguments

formula

Two-sided native mixed-model formula with one grouping column, for example count ~ habitat + (1 | site). Gaussian models also support one block of numeric random slopes such as (1 + habitat | site). Other families allow one random intercept. Use explicit predictors (no .) and formula offsets. The response is a data column, or cbind(successes, failures) for grouped binomial data with positive trial counts.

data

Raw data frame with unique row names. The names identify rows in the split plan and, if supplied, in the prepared raw-cell buffers.

folds

Named list of explicit analysis and assessment row-ID splits. Use grouped_cv_folds() or spatial_cv_folds() to hold out entire groups. Use explicit splits within groups, such as later visits, for existing-group prediction.

family

Character response family. Choose "gaussian" (identity, default), "poisson" (log), "binomial" (logit), "nbinom2" (log), or "Gamma" (log).

prediction

Character prediction target. "new_group" (default) predicts groups absent from training, so each assessment group must have no analysis rows in that split, and its prediction averages over the fitted distribution of group effects. "existing_group" predicts new observations of groups seen in training, so every assessment group must have analysis rows in that split, and its prediction conditions on them.

kernel_inputs

Optional raw-cell multiScaleR_data object for estimating the scales of effect from the analysis rows by native refits. The default NULL fits the supplied formula without scale optimization.

optim_args

Named list of extra serial multiScale_optim() controls. Use only with kernel_inputs. profile_control and the arguments this function sets itself are reserved.

metrics

Character vector of "neg_log_score", "rmse", "mae", or "brier" (binomial only). By default, report the joint group log score and RMSE, or the joint group log score and Brier score for binomial responses. The log score is summed across assessment groups and divided by the number of assessment rows. Binomial RMSE and MAE compare the expected success probability with the observed fraction of successes. The Brier score averages the squared probability error over trials.

control

A glmmTMB::glmmTMBControl() list for the native analysis fits. The default NULL uses glmmTMBControl().

integration_tol

Relative tolerance for the one-dimensional adaptive integration over the group effect in non-Gaussian models. The default is 1e-8.

keep_fits

Logical. Retain the fitted model of each successfully scored fold. Defaults to FALSE.

Value

A list of class multiScaleR_mixed_cv, which inherits from multiScaleR_cv. summary and metrics hold the pooled and per-fold scores, predictions the integrated response mean of each held-out row, joint_scores the joint log score of each held-out group, and training the coefficients, random-effect covariance, dispersion, and any fitted scales of each fold. Compact selection_records are always kept. A failed fold makes the pooled scores NA. The mixed model section of multiScaleR_cv describes every element.

Details

This function is experimental. Its arguments and results may change in a later release without a deprecation period.

How predictions and scores are made

Mixed CV uses maximum-likelihood fits with constant dispersion and a Gaussian distribution for the group effects. Given the fitted parameters, new groups use the estimated population distribution of effects. Existing groups condition that distribution on their analysis responses. Gaussian response models use exact multivariate normal conditioning. For other families the function integrates over one group intercept with adaptive quadrature. Each assessment group contributes one joint predictive density, because all of its rows share one unknown group effect. Parameter, ecological-scale, and model-selection uncertainty are outside these plug-in predictions. Native fitting, preprocessing, and selection use the analysis observations only.

Compare and select models

Use cv_tab() to compare complete results with the same observation support, group assignments, prediction target, and splits. A joint group score is not on the same footing as the per-observation scores of cross_validate_glm(), so the two cannot be mixed. Use select_cv() to evaluate a training information-criterion selection rule. Its sample size is the native number of analysis observations. Estimated covariance parameters count toward the penalty, and integrated group effects do not count individually. vignette("v08-cross-validation", package = "multiScaleR") shows new-site and later-visit designs.

See also

cross_validate(), cross_validate_field(), cv_tab(), select_cv(), and multiScaleR_cv.

Examples

if (requireNamespace("glmmTMB", quietly = TRUE)) {
  surveys <- glmmTMB::Salamanders
  # Hold out whole sites, so every prediction is for a new site
  folds <- grouped_cv_folds(surveys$site, k = 3, ids = rownames(surveys))
  # One fold keeps the example fast
  cv <- cross_validate_mixed(count ~ spp + (1 | site), surveys,
    folds[1], family = "poisson")
  cv$summary   # joint log score per held-out row, and RMSE in counts
}
#>          metric estimate                        unit n_assessment n_scored
#> 1 neg_log_score 1.930772 joint_group_density_per_row          224      224
#> 2          rmse 3.293890                    response          224      224
#>   weight_sum complete
#> 1        224     TRUE
#> 2        224     TRUE
